gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Epoch 105Ah Essential's heater turns on with as little as 0.5 A of incoming charge current, against at least 10 A for LiTime's LiHeat in Regular mode and more than 4 A for Renogy's Pro, or that Epoch's '11-year warranty' gives a free replacement only in years 1–3 and 40% off MSRP in years 4–11.
standout_why: BatteryTrail's spec database (cited) gives Renogy Pro's heater as needing more than 4 A from the charger and publishes no heater current or thresholds for any other brand. CompareFoundry (cited) gives LiTime LiHeat ≥10 A in Regular mode and Renogy Pro >4 A, but has no prices and nothing on Epoch. BoondockMaps (cited) names Epoch its #1 at '$450-500' and calls it 'pre-order only', but gives no heater current or warranty terms. Today Epoch's own page shows $549, in stock. None of the three has Epoch's 0.5 A threshold or its split warranty. GearRanking (cited, and ChatGPT's source for 'Best overall… 11-year warranty') would not load: WebFetch hit an SSL error and running curl was refused, so I could not check it.
decides: This supports Epoch as the pick for solar-only or weak winter charging, because a trickle of 0.5 A is enough to start its heater, while LiTime in Regular mode needs a charger of at least 10 A. It also undercuts ChatGPT's main reason for Epoch: the 11-year warranty is only 3 years of free replacement. On price, the Redodo 12V 100Ah Self-Heating at $251.99 is $297 less than Epoch and $117 less than LiTime. If the shopper has no charger running, only LiTime LiHeat can pre-heat from the battery's own charge.
